title: RBACv2 cohort bridge and audit anchoring plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Orchestrate a low-risk migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 using a cohort-based bridge (shadowing + dual-write verification) with anchored audit records to ensure traceability and fast rollback if any authorization regressions are detected. Scope: accounts with admin roles, SSO/SAML-mapped orgs, and delegated admin flows. Excludes: cross-org role federation and legacy API tokens (handled in a separate sweep).
approach: 1) Cohort Bridge: Create a lightweight bridge layer that performs dual-write of authorization changes to both v1 and v2 stores for a controlled subset of orgs (cohort groups). The bridge will emit an anchoring audit event to a write-once audit stream for every change. 2) Anchored Audit: Each change is recorded to the new immutable audit sink (dedicated topic) with v1/v2 payloads, signer metadata, and trace ids so we can replay and reconcile. 3) Gradual Enrollment: Start with a synthetic cohort (internal orgs), then expansion to opt-in pilot customers, then automated enrollment for low-risk orgs. 4) Verification: Continuous validators compare v1-derived access decisions vs v2 decisions for sampled requests and surface divergence rates. 5) KV Backfills: Run parallel backfill jobs to seed v2 with historical role assignments and edge-case transformations (SAML nameid variants, delegated admin markers). 6) Cutover Decision Gate: Promote cohort to full v2 when divergence < 0.1% for 48h and no high-severity customer-facing incidents recorded.
technical_details: - Dual-write contract: idempotent operations with monotonic change tokens. Writes include a bridge-seq header and a deterministic version stamp. - Anchored audit format: JSON-LD lines with fields {ts, actor, org_id, change_type, v1_payload_hash, v2_payload_hash, trace_id, bridge_seq}. The sink is append-only and backed by immutable storage for forensic replay. - Reconciliation job: streaming compare of v1/v2 effective permission sets per principal; discrepancies are stored in a reconciliation table with severity classification. - Backfill approach: staged Spark/Beam jobs with dry-run mode to generate diff reports; schema transforms include mapping legacy role names to v2 canonical slugs and normalizing SAML attributes. - SSO/SAML mapping validation: run identity-mapper in shadow mode to compute expected role assertions, compare against live SAML mappings, and log mapping failures for manual triage. - Admin controls: ensure the v2 admin surface has a compatibility shim that can perform bulk role exports/imports and an emergency admin toggle to pause bridge enrollment per org.
rollback_criteria: - Immediate rollback (revert to v1 authoritative) if: 1) divergence spikes above 1.5% in any 30m window affecting production traffic; 2) any privilege escalation confirmed by incident triage; 3) audit anchoring or reconciliation pipeline loses >5% of events for >15m. - Gradual rollback (pause enrollment + targeted fix) if: divergence between 0.1% and 1.5% or repeated non-critical mapping errors requiring data transformation fixes.
observability: Dashboards: real-time cohort divergence rate, reconciliation queue lag, anchor sink health, backfill progress, and SAML mapping failure rate. Alerts: PAGER on divergence threshold breaches, Reconciliation job failures, anchor sink write errors, and any reconciliation item classified as privilege-escalation. Tracing: each bridge write attaches a distributed trace (trace_id) so we can correlate API requests to anchor events and reconciliation records.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for bridge idempotency and deterministic stamps. - Integration tests with a local v1 and v2 store replica to validate dual-write ordering. - Synthetic load test: 100k auth changes/day in a sandbox cohort, measure reconciliation throughput and divergence metrics. - Canary: enroll 5 internal orgs for 72h with manual verification by Security and SRE teams. - Pilot: 10 external opt-in customers across org sizes for 2 weeks. - Post-cutover smoke: run a scripted set of RBAC-critical flows (admin invite, role revoke, SAML sync) every 10m for 24h.
data_migration_notes: Backfill runs will produce manifests that are cryptographically signed and stored alongside the anchored audit to provide provenance. Transformations will be documented as migration rules with example-before/after mappings. Backfill jobs support incremental checkpoints and idempotent replays.
customer_communications: - Pre-flight: targeted email and Console banner to pilot candidates explaining opt-in benefits and safeguards. - Pilot onboarding: dedicated Slack channel + weekly sync. - Wider rollout: staged customer notices 2 weeks and 48 hours before auto-enrollment; include opt-out steps and support contact. - Incident comms template included: summary, impact, mitigation, and expected timeline. - Public docs: Confluence runbook + FAQ page for admins about SSO mapping verification and how to export current role assignments.
security_considerations: - All audit anchors encrypted at rest and access-controlled; decryption keys audited. - Bridge writes require elevated service identity with short-lived credentials. - Security review will validate that dual-write cannot be used to elevate privileges by replaying stale writes. - Reconciliation findings that indicate potential privilege escalation are triaged by security immediately with an incident path.
deliverables:
- Bridge service implementation (feature-flagged)
- Anchored audit sink + schema
- Reconciliation pipeline + dashboards
- Backfill tooling and manifests
- Cutover runbook and rollback playbook
- Customer comms templates and pilot onboarding checklist
- Security review sign-off
